Q: 504 (Outdated Optimize Dep) while using react-vite A:

None of the suggested fixes worked in my case. The actual issue was that my project was missing both client/.env.example and client/.env, so all my VITE_* environment variables were undefined. After creating the .env file with the required variables and restarting the Vite dev server, the 504 (Outdated Optimize Dep) error disappeared for me.

Q: Cannot read property 'subscribe' of undefined angular A:

Always return an Observable from the service and let the component subscribe. Use operators like shareReplay(1) , expose a BehaviourSubject as asObservavble() to cache the last value without manual subscription.

Q: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.json.JSONObject A:

Using gradle and eclipse I worked around this problem by explicitly specifying the directory of the referenced libraries in the run command java -cp build/libs/jarFile.jar:build/libs/* projectName.mainClassName this is assuming the referenced .jar files are in build/libs/*

Q: How to modify the TYPO3 13 bootstrap_package 16 CSS in a site package? A:

After asking Google AI I finally got a good answer and by accident its example solved also the problem with the overriding characters of the drop down menu. And not bg-opacity is needed at all.

The right place for putting the CSS variables since TYPO3 13 is the file settings.yaml .

my_site_package/Configuration/Sets/MyDefaultSet/Extensions/BootstrapPackage/settings.yaml

This is an example path of my_site_package extension. You can use a different path and will have your own site package extension name.

plugin:
  bootstrap_package:
    settings:
        scss:
            # set the background color of the drop down box
            dropdown-bg: '#ffffff'

With this entry the drop down boxes have a white background which are not transparent after clicking on them. The transparency is only active after scrolling the text of the main context upwards. This is fine. After each click on the menu entries the drop down box will immediately lose its transparency and the menu texts are well readable again.
And by this way you can even add SCSS variables of Bootstrap which are not included in the TYPO3 bootstrap extension. You only need to clear the TYPO3 cache in the back end module (Flush TYPO3 and PHP Cache) once to get it immediately working.
An alternative way for former TYPO3 versions would be a constants.typoscript file instead of it.

plugin.bootstrap_package.settings.scss {
    primary = #eb3e4a
    secondary = #013859
}

However I see no way how to introduce the SCSS variable `dropdown-bg` into a constants file I stop here. The settings.yaml works for my needs. A settings.definitions.yaml could be used for the constants editor.

Q: Using group by on multiple columns A:

Here I am going to explain not only the GROUP clause use, but also the Aggregate functions use.

The GROUP BY clause is used in conjunction with the aggregate functions to group the result-set by one or more columns. e.g.:

-- GROUP BY with one parameter:
SELECT column_name, AGGREGATE_FUNCTION(column_name)
FROM table_name
WHERE column_name operator value
GROUP BY column_name;

-- GROUP BY with two parameters:
SELECT
    column_name1,
    column_name2,
    AGGREGATE_FUNCTION(column_name3)
FROM
    table_name
GROUP BY
    column_name1,
    column_name2;

I wrote Introduction to the Structured Query Language (SQL) – In Only a Few Pages, a concise beginner's guide to SQL. https://www.amazon.com/Introduction-Structured-Query-Language-Pages/dp/B0GP6ZYJMX

Remember this order:

  1. SELECT (is used to select data from a database)

  2. FROM (clause is used to list the tables)

  3. WHERE (clause is used to filter records)

  4. GROUP BY (clause can be used in a SELECT statement to collect data across multiple records and group the results by one or more columns)

  5. HAVING (clause is used in combination with the GROUP BY clause to restrict the groups of returned rows to only those whose the condition is TRUE)

  6. ORDER BY (keyword is used to sort the result-set)

You can use all of these if you are using aggregate functions, and this is the order that they must be set, otherwise you can get an error.

Aggregate Functions are:

MIN() returns the smallest value in a given column

MAX() returns the maximum value in a given column.

SUM() returns the sum of the numeric values in a given column

AVG() returns the average value of a given column

COUNT() returns the total number of values in a given column

COUNT(*) returns the number of rows in a table

SQL script examples about using aggregate functions:

Let's say we need to find the sale orders whose total sale is greater than $950. We combine the HAVING clause and the GROUP BY clause to accomplish this:

SELECT 
    orderId, SUM(unitPrice * qty) Total
FROM
    OrderDetails
GROUP BY orderId
HAVING Total > 950;

Counting all orders and grouping them customerID and sorting the result ascendant. We combine the COUNT function and the GROUP BY, ORDER BY clauses and ASC:

SELECT 
    customerId, COUNT(*)
FROM
    Orders
GROUP BY customerId
ORDER BY COUNT(*) ASC;

Retrieve the category that has an average Unit Price greater than $10, using AVG function combine with GROUP BY and HAVING clauses:

SELECT 
    categoryName, AVG(unitPrice)
FROM
    Products p
INNER JOIN
    Categories c ON c.categoryId = p.categoryId
GROUP BY categoryName
HAVING AVG(unitPrice) > 10;

Getting the less expensive product by each category, using the MIN function in a subquery:

SELECT categoryId,
       productId,
       productName,
       unitPrice
FROM Products p1
WHERE unitPrice = (
                SELECT MIN(unitPrice)
                FROM Products p2
                WHERE p2.categoryId = p1.categoryId)

The following will show you how to select the most recent date item "productDate", using MAX function in a subquery:

SELECT categoryId,
       productId,
       productName,
       unitPrice,
       productDate
FROM Products p1
WHERE productDate= (
                  SELECT MAX(productDate) 
                  FROM Products p2
                  WHERE p2.categoryId = p1.categoryId)

The following statement groups rows with the same values in both categoryId and productId columns:

SELECT 
    categoryId, categoryName, productId, SUM(unitPrice)
FROM
    Products p
INNER JOIN
    Categories c ON c.categoryId = p.categoryId
GROUP BY categoryId, productId

To answer a question: - what if use GROUP BY but no aggregate function? The answer is: We can also use the GROUP BY without applying the Aggregate function. Here is an example where we are grouping by categoryId:

SELECT categoryId,
       productId,
       productName,
       unitPrice
FROM Products
GROUP BY categoryId

Q: Why Makefile results in an error with canonical name? A:

The warning message is misleading. Note that Automake does not complain about libhelpers_a_SOURCES or libhelpers_a_CXXFLAGS, which confirms what you already knew from the rules for canonical name construction: libhelpers_a is the canonical name corresponding to your libhelpers.a.

The actual problem is that static libraries have no link step, so *_LDFLAGS does not apply to them. The warning message is too generic here; it would be on point if it were reduced to speak only about programs, not libraries:

warning: variable 'libhelpers_a_LDFLAGS' is defined but no program has 'libhelpers_a' as canonical name (possible typo)

Of course, an even more specific message would be even better.

Resolve the warning by removing the variable.
